newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices unmoved pre-holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices unmoved pre-holiday.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices were stagnant at midday after a jump November new home sales and a rise in December consumer confidence walloped U.S. Treasuries in the last trading day of 1996.

"There's no trading going on. There's no interest, nobody's doing anything," a municipal trader said. "There were some kind of flat trades to yesterday first thing in the morning, and then when it started ticking down that really removed any possibility of getting anything done."

New U.S. single-family home sales jumped 14.2 percent in November to a 772,000 annualized rate, exceeding the consensus forecast in a Reuters poll of 731,000. In addition, the Conference Board reported that consumer confidence rose to 113.8 in December from a revised reading of 109.5 in November.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 1-4/32 at 98-9/32 to yield 6.63 percent. In debt futures, the March municipal contract was down 25/32 at 116-9/32. The March T-bond contract was down 1-1/32 at 112-27/32. The MOB was 110 ticks.

Looking ahead, a trader said early January's "traditional drought of new issues" should help municipals outperform the government market. But how much January re-investment money ends up in the municipal market remains to be seen, he said.
"I think there will be some good retail interest for certain states, (but) a lot depends on whether people put the money to work or sit on it," the trader said.
